title: Sensex Surges 1,419 Points as Crude Crashes After US Midterm Sweep
excerpt: The Sensex jumped 1,418.56 points to 78,719.96 and the Nifty rose past 24,300 on November 5, as Brent crude fell close to 10 per cent to around $94 after Democrats swept the US midterms.
body:
• The Sensex surged 1,418.56 points, or 1.84 per cent, to 78,719.96 in early trade on Thursday, November 5, while the Nifty 50 jumped 400 points to 24,360.70, extending the winning streak to a sixth consecutive session.
  • Brent crude fell close to 10 per cent to around $94 a barrel after Democrats swept the US midterm elections, raising hopes of de-escalation in the US-Iran conflict.
  • Foreign institutional investors bought ₹7,284 crore of equities in the previous session alone and ₹20,834 crore over four sessions, according to reporting cited by The Hindu BusinessLine.
  • For investors: lower crude eases India's inflation and import-bill pressure, but analysts quoted in the coverage warned the oil fall is driven by expectations, not a confirmed settlement, so the rally remains exposed to any setback in West Asia talks.

Indian equities opened sharply higher on Thursday, November 5, as a crash in crude oil prices and a decisive result in the US midterm elections lifted sentiment across sectors. The Sensex surged 1,418.56 points to 78,719.96, after opening at 78,910.94 against a previous close of 77,301.40, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The Nifty 50 opened at 24,378.05, against a previous close of 23,960.60, and was up 400 points to 24,360.70.

Upstox, citing exchange data, put the opening move even higher, reporting the Sensex at 78,910.94 at the opening bell, up 2 per cent, before it hit a morning high of 78,922.44, a rise of 1,621.04 points. The Nifty hit an early high of 24,391.95 in that reporting.

Crude was the main driver

Both reports identified crude as the primary trigger. BusinessLine said Brent crude dropped close to 10 per cent to around $94 a barrel following the Democratic sweep. Upstox said Brent crashed 11 per cent to a low of $93.50 a barrel in morning trade on November 5, from an intraday high of $104.96 on Wednesday, and was trading at $93.84 a barrel at 9:52 a.m. IST, according to Investing.com data cited by Upstox.

For India, a major oil importer, cheaper crude directly affects inflation expectations, fuel-import costs and the current account. That is why an oil move of this size moves the whole market, not only energy stocks.

Wall Street and flows added support

Wall Street rose sharply after the midterm results. BusinessLine reported the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged over 3 per cent, its strongest post-midterm performance in over four decades, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained over 1.4 per cent each. US 10-year Treasury yields fell to approximately 4.87 to 4.89 per cent, the dollar posted its worst daily performance in two months, and the Indian rupee strengthened for a fourth straight session, gaining 10 paise to close at ₹94.64 against the dollar, BusinessLine reported.

Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, told BusinessLine the fall in crude was happening at a time when "the Indian economy is showing great resilience and corporate earnings are showing significant improvement." He said that shift had "completely changed the FII's stance towards India," with foreign investors buying ₹20,834 crore over the previous four trading sessions in the cash market.

"The Indian economy is showing great resilience and corporate earnings are showing significant improvement."

— Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments

Who gained, who lagged

Among Nifty 50 stocks, BusinessLine reported Shriram Finance led the gainers, rising 6.35 per cent to ₹966.45, followed by IndiGo at ₹5,418.10, up 5.39 per cent. Asian Paints climbed 4.56 per cent to ₹2,528.50, Tata Motors' preferred variant gained 4.13 per cent to ₹290.00 and Maruti Suzuki rose 4.06 per cent to ₹12,482. On the losing side, Apollo Hospitals fell 2.19 per cent to ₹8,411, ONGC dropped 1.85 per cent to ₹230.66 and Cipla slipped 0.56 per cent to ₹1,394.10.

What to watch

The caution in the coverage was explicit. Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth, told BusinessLine crude's fall "remains driven by expectations rather than a confirmed settlement or full restoration of energy flows, leaving crude vulnerable to any setback in negotiations." Sachin Gupta, VP–Technical Research at Choice Broking, noted the Nifty had sustained its position above the 200-day exponential moving average near 23,904, with the relative strength index at 68.55, though he flagged possible near-term profit booking. For diaspora investors holding India funds, Thursday's move is therefore a sentiment and oil story first — its durability depends on whether crude stays near $94 and foreign buying continues.
